items.title: AI-powered ECG assessments may improve heart transplant rejection warnings
items.excerpt: An AI model reading routine ECGs flagged acute cellular rejection in heart transplant recipients; researchers plan to test it in more patients at several transplant centers. (Off-list exception: sister title of radiologybusiness.com; no on-list fresh AI-ECG story.)

items.title: AI flags heart failure patients at risk of functional decline
items.excerpt: A machine-learning model identifies hospitalized heart failure patients likely to lose functional independence after discharge, shifting prediction from survival to quality of life. (Off-list exception.)

items.title: Robotic therapy for stroke patients
items.excerpt: An adaptive physical rehab system uses generative AI to learn from physical therapists and offer personalized support to stroke patients.

items.title: Can one photo of your face reveal how ill you are?
items.excerpt: US researchers report a foundation AI model (FAHR-Face, Lancet Digital Health) that may help doctors judge how ill a patient is from a single photograph of their face.

items.title: GUARD-LGG: a glioma upfront AI-driven radiotherapy response decipher for lower-grade glioma
items.excerpt: An AI model predicts, before treatment, how lower-grade glioma patients will respond to radiotherapy - a prediction that clinicians currently lack.

items.title: Expertise modulates automation bias and sentinel behavior in human-AI collaborative diagnosis of neonatal pneumoperitoneum
items.excerpt: Tests the assumption that AI sensitivity plus clinician oversight adds up: in neonatal pneumoperitoneum diagnosis, clinician expertise shaped automation bias and whether readers caught AI errors.

items.title: Reinforcement learning for repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation protocol selection in treatment-resistant depression
items.excerpt: A reinforcement-learning approach recommends rTMS/iTBS protocols for treatment-resistant depression, where clinicians lack evidence-based guidance on choosing among protocols.

items.title: LLMs mostly avoid unnecessary care in Choosing Wisely tests
items.excerpt: Tested against Choosing Wisely recommendations, LLMs suggested potentially unnecessary care in about 5% of responses, many of them thyroid ultrasound tests.

items.title: Why teaching AI about symmetry could make prenatal diagnosis more reliable
items.excerpt: A new AI model called E(3)-Pose helps capture high-resolution images of a fetus's head to improve early detection of developmental anomalies during pregnancy.

items.title: AI prescriptions: App to issue drugs without doctors' oversight in the US
items.excerpt: Utah authorised startup Nolla Health's AI to prescribe acne drugs from facial scans via its Nolla Derm app; doctors approve each script at first, but later phases let the AI prescribe independently.

history_match.title: Utah approves slew of health AI pilots for drug management, women's health

items.title: Measuring What Medical AI Can Actually Do
items.excerpt: Stanford researchers look back on three years of building progressively harder, more realistic benchmarks of medical AI on real clinical tasks and what they learned.

items.title: Why AI Isn't Ready to Tackle Our Convoluted Genomes
items.excerpt: DNA is dynamic rather than a fixed set of instructions, and AI models don't yet have the data to decode it - a limit for AI-driven genomic diagnosis.

items.title: AI-Assisted Molecular Review Refines SMO Inhibitor Candidacy in SHH Medulloblastoma
items.excerpt: NEJM AI case study: an AI-assisted molecular review refined whether a patient with SHH-subgroup medulloblastoma was a candidate for SMO-inhibitor therapy. (Date via Crossref created.)

items.title: Clinical AI in 2025-2026 - Six Themes from the SAIL Year in Review
items.excerpt: NEJM AI perspective distilling six themes in clinical AI deployment from the SAIL year-in-review. (Date via Crossref created.)

items.title: 'AI sandboxes' are all the rage. Advocates scramble to control their future
items.excerpt: STAT Health Tech: the groups vying to shape regulations governing state health-AI sandboxes such as Utah's.
